messages:
support-alex: FYI — escalation from Customer MD (AcmePayments). They see spikes of 504s and occasional 502s hitting hosted inference gateway since ~09:10 PT. Says it started after a traffic burst. They attached curl repro and logs.

customer-md: repro: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-llama-7b\",\"input\":\"hello\"}' --max-time 30
getting HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout mostly after a ~20s wait. Happening ~2-3% of requests intermittently.

ops-bot: alert: gateway.queue_depth > 90% for 3m on prod (route: /v1/generate) — link: https://grafana/redwood/d/queue/gateway-queue (pager: paged)

deploy-bot: deploy: feat/adaptive-batching rolled to prod 2026-03-15T07:08:12Z by jamal-eng (deploy id: dpl-20260315-78)

maya-oncall: thanks, pulling metrics. can you confirm tenant id and route? also any recent config changes for batching/queue depth?

support-alex: tenant: tenant_acme, route: /v1/generate, spikes started ~09:08 PT. customer says spike correlated with a ramping job from their end (sustained fanout). no other config changes on their side.

jamal-eng: that deploy is the one that changes batching heuristics + queue depth enforcement (we lowered per-route max queue depth to 500 to avoid huge memory use). rolled 07:08 — matches timeline.

sre-lina: looking at batcher logs — continuous-batcher backlog shows steady growth and tail latencies for kv-cache hits drop. samples: 
```
2026-03-15T09:09:02Z batcher INFO backlog_size=612 queue_depth=612 avg_batch_window_ms=45
2026-03-15T09:09:07Z batcher WARN tail_latency_p95_ms=7600 tail_latency_p99_ms=18200
```
This feels like queue depth cap + continuous-batching backlog causing tail timeouts (requests waiting in queue > client timeout).

maya-oncall: agree. quick mitigation options: 1) raise per-route queue_depth limit to 1000 or 1500 temporarily; 2) roll back adaptive-batching deploy; 3) enable emergency early-reject (return 429 instead of letting requests tail out). Which should we do now?

support-alex: customer asks for fastest fix; prefers fewer 5xx/504s even if they get 429s.

jamal-eng: I can bump queue limit now via central-config; minimal risk. I will also open rollback PR in parallel.

maya-oncall: go for bump + rolling restart on gateway pods. please monitor p95/p99 and errors. I'll notify customer.

jamal-eng: running command to patch config (prod):
```
# patch central config to increase per-route queue_depth
PATCH /configs/global HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "routes": {
    "/v1/generate": { "max_queue_depth": 1000 }
  }
}
```
Applied. triggering config reload on gateway.

ops-bot: action: config.reload triggered for gateway (cfg-20260315-09-15)

maya-oncall: doing rolling restart on gateway pods: kubectl rollout restart deployment/gateway-prod -n prod

deploy-bot: rollout: gateway-prod restarted by maya-oncall (rollout id: r-20260315-912)

sre-lina: observing metrics after patch: queue_depth dropped from 620->240 over 40s, tail error rate decreased. p95 latency down from 7.6s -> 280ms. 504s trending to 0.6% from 2.8%.

customer-md: confirming — saw immediate improvement, 504s dropped. thanks.

maya-oncall: root cause summary (short): the adaptive-batching change lowered per-route queue cap to 500 which during customer ramp caused continuous-batcher backlog and requests to wait past client timeouts, producing 504s/502s. We mitigated by raising max_queue_depth to 1000 and rolling gateway pods.

jamal-eng: follow-ups: 1) ENG-4572 created to revert or adjust adaptive-batching defaults and add per-tenant safety controls (owner: jamal-eng) 2) add a canary constraint so next deploy will gradually adjust queue caps with circuit-breaker 3) update runbook to include raising queue depth + early-reject option.

maya-oncall: created incident ticket INC-20260315-03 to track mitigation and postmortem. assigning jamal-eng and sre-lina.

support-alex: communicated mitigation to customer and offered dedicated capacity options. customer accepted temporary fix and requested follow-up once permanent change in place.

jamal-eng: I'll submit a hotfix to change default max_queue_depth back to 1500 for high-throughput routes and add telemetry for queue tail waits. will also attach a test harness to simulate sustained fanout.

sre-lina: postmortem notes: add metric for "queue_wait_time_seconds" per route and alert when >2s for p99; consider API-level 429 early-reject feature.

maya-oncall: closing this thread once ENG-4572 is tracked. great cross-team work. :tada:
